So `pgp20_objects` starts at `pgp33_objects + 7`. Let me look at the DOs that have `get_fn` set (these are the ones that will be read from the card):

Looking at the DO tables, DOs 0x00c1, 0x00c2, 0x00c3 do NOT have `get_fn` set (they are NULL). This means they are "un-readable DO or part of a constructed DO". They get their data from being children of a constructed DO (0x0073) which is enumerated via TLV parsing.

So the flow is:
1. `pgp_get_blob(card, priv->mf, 0x006e, &blob6e)` - reads DO 0x006e (constructed, has `sc_get_data` as get_fn)
2. `pgp_get_blob(card, blob6e, 0x0073, &blob73)` - reads DO 0x0073 under 0x006e (constructed, no get_fn)
3. For DO 0x0073, since it has no get_fn, `pgp_read_blob` returns success without reading
4. Then `pgp_enumerate_blob` is called on 0x0073, which parses its data as TLV
5. But wait - 0x0073 has no data yet. Let me re-check...

Actually, looking more carefully at `pgp_enumerate_blob`:
- It calls `pgp_read_blob` first
- If the blob has no get_fn, `pgp_read_blob` returns SC_SUCCESS without setting data
- Then `pgp_enumerate_blob` tries to parse `blob->data` which is NULL

Wait, but DO 0x006e has `sc_get_data` as get_fn. So when we read 0x006e, it sends an APDU to the card and gets back data. Then when we enumerate 0x006e, it parses the TLV data and creates child blobs including 0x0073. Then when we read 0x0073, it has no get_fn, so it just returns. But 0x0073's data was already set during enumeration of 0x006e.
